title: Chaos and Diffusion in Twisted Bilayer Graphene
abstract: We numerically analyze chaos and diffusion in experimentally-relevant models of twisted bilayer graphene. Our results indicate that finite systems at both commensurate and incommensurate rotation angles exhibit chaos. We compute the Thouless energy of the system at intermediate twist angles to further understand the diffusive processes associated with the chaotic nature of the spectrum. We find that the mean free path of the non-interacting electrons scales with the system size, which is consistent with diffusive processes caused by border-induced scattering. In summary, our results show the role of borders as a experimentally relevant single-particle scattering mechanism, which is much stronger than in single-layer graphene and induces chaos and diffusion regardless of the rotation angle and the lattice commensurability.
summary: This work numerically analyzes chaos and diffusion in twisted bilayer graphene, demonstrating that the system exhibits quantum chaos even at large twist angles. The key finding is that border-induced scattering acts as a powerful single-particle mechanism, inducing diffusive behavior regardless of lattice commensurability. This highlights the crucial role of sample boundaries in determining electronic transport properties.
main_problem: The study investigates the emergence of quantum chaos and diffusive transport mechanisms within finite-sized Twisted Bilayer Graphene (TBG) flakes.
main_result: Chaos is robustly induced in TBG systems regardless of lattice commensurability or rotation angle, with border scattering identified as a dominant single-particle mechanism causing diffusion.
method: The analysis employs numerical diagonalization of the tight-binding Hamiltonian and uses Random Matrix Theory diagnostics (like level spacing ratios) alongside Thouless energy scaling to characterize spectral statistics.
model_or_system: The system is Twisted Bilayer Graphene modeled by a tight-binding Hamiltonian. The study examines flakes with both commensurate and incommensurate twist angles, focusing on the role of boundaries.

important_parameters: Twist angle ($	heta$), system size ($N$), and the nature of scattering (border-induced vs. intrinsic).
main_assumptions: The analysis often assumes random sliding between layers for comparison, and specific energy ranges are focused on for robust averaging.

paper_structure: The paper progresses by establishing the model (Hamiltonian), applying chaos diagnostics (level statistics vs. GOE/Poisson) across different angles, quantifying diffusion via Thouless energy scaling, and concluding that boundary effects dominate the chaotic behavior.
why_interesting: The findings on how structural imperfections (borders) induce universal quantum chaotic behavior in a 2D material are highly relevant to understanding open quantum systems where boundaries play a critical role.
